◳Baltorhardening ← The engine Facts that refresh, not rot
Engine component · hardening

A copied number goes stale. A hardened fact refreshes.

Hardening is the stage that keeps context current. Most systems copy a volatile value — a rate, a threshold, a deadline — into a doc or a vector store, where it silently rots the moment the source changes. Baltor turns that value into a refreshable object anchored to its source handle: it tracks freshness, and re-verifies the moment the source moves. Pick a volatile fact:

Static copy vs hardened object

Same fact · two ways to store it

Freshness, tracked

The hardened object knows how current it is

When the source changes

Change-data-capture → re-verify → reconcile, automatically
Hardening beside the rest. Hardening (internally, anti-fragility) is one stage — a refreshed fact is then reconciled (against any conflicting source), enhanced (citation re-attached), optimized and verified before it’s served. The point isn’t that the value never changes; it’s that when the world changes, the context follows instead of silently lying. See the guided demos for the full pipeline and the reconciliation deep-dive for what happens when a refresh surfaces a conflict.
